items.passage: 'Keep it until we reach Albuquerque,' Ahanu said, pressing the folded bills into Takoda's hand as the train rocked through the dark. Takoda had been found two days earlier, sunburned and turned around in the canyons, and now he owed the ranger both the fare and the afternoon Ahanu had given up to escort him home. He tried to refuse, but Ahanu only shrugged. Watching him, Takoda realized the ranger did not think of the money as a loan at all; he spoke of it the way one speaks of water shared on a trail, something meant to be passed along rather than counted. Takoda's insistence on writing down an exact sum began to seem ______, a habit of bookkeeping that missed the point of what had been offered.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: gracious
deceitful
urgent
misplaced
items.explanation: Ahanu는 돈을 빌려준 것이 아니라 산길에서 물을 나누듯 건네는 것으로 여긴다는 단서가 앞에 있다. 빈칸 뒤의 '베푼 것의 요점을 놓친 장부 습관'이라는 설명과 연결하면, 정확한 액수를 적으려는 Takoda의 고집은 상황에 맞지 않는 것이다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 고집을 긍정적으로 평가해 문맥과 반대이고, B는 속이려는 의도가 지문에 없으며, C는 서두름과 관련된 단서가 없다.

items.passage: Three rules governed my grandfather's lighthouse station above Valparaiso: wind the lamp at dusk, log every ship, and never speak of money. At his funeral, my cousin Camila kept to the third rule so faithfully that I almost missed what she had done. Only later, reading the station's ledger, did I learn that for six winters she had paid the keeper's wages herself, sending the sums through a lawyer so that no one in the family would know. When I confronted her on the gallery, wind tugging at our black coats, she waved the matter off. 'Amelie, look at the gulls,' she said, and changed the subject. Her generosity, I understood, was deliberately ______: she had arranged everything so that gratitude would never find her.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: inconspicuous
extravagant
reluctant
temporary
items.explanation: Camila는 변호사를 통해 몰래 임금을 보냈고, 추궁당하자 화제를 돌렸으며, 감사가 자신에게 닿지 않도록 모든 것을 꾸몄다. 이 단서들을 연결하면 그녀의 너그러움은 일부러 눈에 띄지 않게 한 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 과시적이라는 뜻이라 숨긴 행동과 맞지 않는다. C는 그녀가 마지못해 도왔다는 근거가 없고, D는 여섯 해 겨울 동안 계속된 사실과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Once, in a seed-saving cooperative at the edge of Glasgow, two siblings named Malek and Niamh kept a shop that sold fewer packets each year. Long before, Malek had borrowed a brass sieve from the cooperative's elders and never brought it back. Every season he meant to return it, and every season he found another use for it: sifting barley, cleaning poppy seed, rescuing a spilled jar of beans. When the elders finally came asking, Niamh expected them to be angry. Instead, they examined the worn mesh, bright from years of handling, and declared that the sieve had been ______ rather than kept; a tool that had worked so hard, they said, belonged to whoever had given it work.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: hidden
earned
damaged
forgotten
items.explanation: Malek은 체를 해마다 여러 용도로 써 왔고, 장로들은 닳아 반짝이는 체를 보고 화를 내지 않았다. 또 '그토록 열심히 일한 도구는 일을 준 사람의 것'이라는 말이 이어지므로, 체는 그냥 가진 것이 아니라 쓰임으로 얻어 낸 것이라는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 숨겼다는 근거가 없고, C는 '닳은' 표현에서 나온 오답이지만 장로들의 긍정적 평가와 맞지 않는다. D는 Malek이 매 계절 돌려줄 생각을 했다는 내용과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Promises cost money. Aunt Consuelo said so every evening as she counted the day's coins at their food cart on the promenade in Oaxaca, and Tomoe, sixteen and tired of hearing it, had stopped arguing. That afternoon Tomoe had told a small boy, who lingered by the cart without a peso, that she would save him a tamal at closing. Consuelo had overheard and clicked her tongue. Now the sun was sinking into the Pacific, the last tamal sat wrapped in its husk, and a customer was holding out a bill for it. Consuelo took the tamal from the steamer, looked down the promenade at the boy hurrying toward them, and set it in Tomoe's hands instead. 'A promise is also a debt,' she said quietly, and for once she did not count anything.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From playful teasing to open anger, as Consuelo scolds Tomoe for giving food away.
From hopeful anticipation to disappointment, as the boy arrives too late for food.
From weary irritation to quiet tenderness, as Consuelo honors Tomoe's promise.
From calm routine to nervous urgency, as Tomoe rushes to sell out before dark.
items.explanation: 앞부분에는 같은 말을 되풀이하는 이모와 지친 Tomoe, 혀를 차는 Consuelo의 반응이 있어 피곤하고 짜증스러운 분위기다. 그러나 손님의 돈 대신 소년을 위해 타말을 건네고 조용히 말하며 처음으로 돈을 세지 않는 장면에서 다정함으로 바뀌므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이모가 꾸짖는 장면이 없고, B는 소년이 늦지 않았으며, D는 서두르는 긴박함이 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage: Krakow slid past the porthole as Harriet bent over the letter at the galley table, the only flat surface on the river barge wide enough for her pattern papers. Stanislav, her apprentice, had translated the client's instructions from Polish, and for an hour they had laughed over the request: a wedding dress cut 'short, like a quick confession.' Harriet called it the strangest order of her career and pinned the hem a scandalous hand above the knee. Then Stanislav, rereading the original, went pale. The word he had rendered as 'short' could also mean 'plain,' and the bride, whose mother had died that spring, wanted nothing that would draw the eye. Harriet set the scissors down without a word and began, slowly, to unpick every pin.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From quiet concentration to frantic panic, as Harriet fears missing a deadline.
From mutual suspicion to trust, as Harriet comes to rely on Stanislav's skill.
From cheerful pride to defiance, as Harriet refuses to change her own design.
From amused curiosity to sober regret, as the error alters the dress's meaning.
items.explanation: 처음에 두 사람은 이상한 주문을 두고 한 시간 동안 웃으며 대담하게 단을 핀으로 고정한다. Stanislav가 원문을 다시 읽고 창백해진 뒤, 상중인 신부가 눈에 띄지 않는 옷을 원했다는 사실이 드러나고 Harriet은 말없이 핀을 뽑는다. 따라서 흥미로운 웃음에서 무거운 후회로 바뀌었다는 D가 정답이다. A는 마감 압박이 없고, B는 처음부터 의심이 없었으며, C는 Harriet이 오히려 디자인을 바꾸기 시작한다.

items.passage:
'Check,' Maya said, though no board lay between us,
only the boarding-house kettle and two cracked cups.
All week the club had whispered of my blunder,
the queen I'd left hanging like wash in the Haifa wind,
and Maya, smug as a bishop, had told it best.
So I, Dvora, came down to the kitchen armed with silence,
ready to answer every pawn of her pity.
But she poured the tea, and slid the sugar toward me,
and said she'd lost the same way once, at twenty,
to a man who never let her forget it.
We sat until the window went blue with morning,
two old rivals, the game between us set down.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the poem?
options: From wary defensiveness to reconciliation, as the rival offers unexpected sympathy.
From triumph to humiliation, as the speaker loses a second game to her rival.
From nostalgia to bitterness, as the speaker recalls a man who mocked her.
From playful banter to cold politeness, as both women hide their true feelings.
items.explanation: 화자 Dvora는 소문을 퍼뜨린 Maya에게 맞서려고 '침묵으로 무장한 채' 부엌에 내려온다. 그러나 'But' 이후 Maya가 차를 따르고 자신도 같은 방식으로 졌던 경험을 털어놓자, 두 사람은 아침까지 함께 앉아 대국을 내려놓는다. 따라서 방어적 긴장에서 화해로 바뀐다는 A가 정답이다. B는 두 번째 대국이 없고, C의 남자는 Maya의 과거 이야기일 뿐 화자의 쓰라림이 아니며, D는 마지막 장면의 친밀함과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
'I keep telling you, Pa, nobody pays for hand-pressing anymore,' CLEMENT says, dropping a basket onto the folding counter of the laundromat in Port of Spain. LINTON, his father, does not answer. He lifts an old charcoal iron from its shelf and sets it heating.
CLEMENT: You'll burn the place down with that relic.
LINTON: (smoothing a white collar) Your grandmother pressed shirts for half of Belmont with this. Every crease told the customer somebody cared.
CLEMENT: (mocking) Every crease told them she couldn't afford a machine.
(LINTON holds out the iron. CLEMENT hesitates, then takes it. He presses one sleeve, clumsy at first, then slower, then slower still.)
CLEMENT: (quietly) It's heavier than I thought.
LINTON: That's the weight of it. She carried it up every hill in Belmont.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From warm nostalgia to open grief, as Linton mourns his late mother aloud.
From scornful dismissal to grudging respect, as Clement feels the craft's weight.
From playful joking to sharp anger, as Linton scolds Clement's clumsiness.
From quiet tension to relief, as Clement agrees to replace the old iron.
items.explanation: Clement는 처음에 손다림질을 아무도 돈 내지 않는 일, 다리미를 '유물'이라 부르며 조롱한다. 직접 다리미를 들고 점점 천천히 다리다가 '생각보다 무겁다'고 조용히 말하는 장면에서 태도가 바뀌고, 아버지의 대답이 그 무게에 할머니의 노고라는 의미를 더한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 Linton이 슬픔을 드러내지 않고, C는 꾸짖는 장면이 없으며, D는 다리미를 바꾸자는 합의가 없다.

items.passage: Two bowls of miso ramen steamed between us in the roadside diner outside Asahikawa, and for the first twenty minutes Judge Sota talked only about procedure. I had clerked for him for three years, and he reminded me that he had misspelled my name, Rohan, on my first evaluation; he wanted to correct the record before he left Hokkaido for good. He listed the filing deadlines I would need to watch under his successor, the drawer that stuck, the bailiff who hated small talk. Then a snowplow rumbled past the window and he stopped mid-sentence. 'I was not a kind judge,' he said, looking at his noodles. 'I hope I was a fair one. You will have to tell me which matters more.' I saw that he had driven three hours not to brief me but to be judged.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From cheerful nostalgia to resentment over the narrator's first evaluation.
From awkward silence to lively debate about the judge's chosen successor.
From brisk, practical instruction to vulnerable self-examination by the judge.
From formal reserve to playful teasing as the judge mocks the old bailiff.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Sota 판사는 기한, 고장 난 서랍, 법정 경위 같은 실무만 나열한다. 제설차가 지나간 뒤 말을 멈추고 자신이 친절한 판사가 아니었다며 공정했기를 바란다고 털어놓는 부분에서 어조가 취약한 자기 성찰로 바뀌므로 C가 정답이다. A는 평가서 오기를 바로잡으려 할 뿐 원망이 없고, B는 후임자를 두고 논쟁하지 않으며, D는 경위에 대한 언급이 놀림이 아니라 업무 정보다.

items.passage: Caio came back on a Tuesday. I was working the night shift at the customs checkpoint outside Vienna, as I had since renting him the flat above my bakery eleven years before, and there he was in the queue, his passport held out as if no time had passed. For four years his rent had arrived each month by mail, no letter attached, while his rooms sat dark. I had rehearsed a speech for this moment: the questions, the overdue repairs, the neighbors' rumors. I stamped his passport with exaggerated care. Then he set something on the counter: the spare key I had given him, wrapped in a handkerchief my mother had embroidered, which I thought had been lost with her belongings. 'She asked me to keep it safe, Lena,' he said. My speech went somewhere I could not follow.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From cheerful surprise to suspicion, as the narrator questions Caio's passport.
From weary routine to anger, as the narrator delivers her rehearsed speech.
From anxious fear to relief, as Caio finally pays all of the overdue rent.
From guarded resentment to stunned emotion, as Caio reveals a tie to her mother.
items.explanation: 화자 Lena는 편지 한 장 없이 사라졌던 세입자에게 할 말을 연습해 두었고, 여권에 일부러 과장되게 도장을 찍으며 서운함을 드러낸다. 그러나 Caio가 어머니의 손수건에 싼 열쇠를 내놓고 어머니의 부탁이었다고 말하자 연습한 말이 사라질 만큼 감정이 흔들린다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 처음부터 반가움이 없고, B는 연습한 말을 결국 하지 못하며, C는 집세가 이미 매달 들어오고 있었다.

items.passage:
Years ago, Achan, you stood with me on our rooftop in Kochi, pinning your work shirts to the line, and told me never to explain our move to Aigerim until she was old enough. I agreed; I was twelve and proud to keep a secret in a language you were still learning. Now Aigerim is ten, and she asks me in English why we left, and I answer her in the cheerful phrases you approved: better schools, a bigger sky. But last week she found your old visa papers folded in the laundry basket, the ones stamped refused twice, and she asked me why you had cried on the phone. I could not invent a cheerful phrase for that. She deserves the true version, told by you, and I am asking you to tell her.
With love, Ananya
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the letter?
options: From fond recollection of a shared promise to an earnest appeal to break it.
From cheerful description to bitter accusation that the father lied to them.
From formal politeness to playful humor about Aigerim's curious questions.
From anxious worry to calm relief, as Ananya resolves to keep the secret.
items.explanation: 편지는 옥상 빨랫줄 앞에서 아버지와 비밀을 약속하던 기억을 다정하게 떠올리며 시작한다. 'But' 이후 동생이 비자 서류를 발견하고 질문하는 사건이 나오면서, Ananya는 아버지가 직접 진실을 말해 달라고 진지하게 요청한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 비난이 아니라 부탁이고, C는 유머가 없으며, D는 비밀을 지키려는 것이 아니라 깨자고 제안하므로 반대다.

items.passage: 'Read the harbor part again,' Yuxuan said, and so I did, sitting cross-legged among the half-strung kites in the old kite-maker's yard in Lisbon where Mother used to work. Our plan had been simple: sell her last kites at the festival, use the money to buy back the letters she had pawned, and finally learn why she left for those three years. Today the plan worked. We sold all nine kites before noon. We bought the bundle back, tied in her blue thread, and we laughed the whole way to the yard. Then we read them. She wrote about the harbor, about missing us, about a doctor she never mentioned. Yuxuan has folded the letters back into their thread. Neither of us has said a word since. I wanted answers; I did not know they would weigh this much. Shanice, before bed
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the diary entry?
options: From quiet grief to renewed hope as the siblings recover their mother's letters.
From buoyant excitement over a successful plan to a heavy, subdued silence.
From anxious doubt to pride as the siblings sell every kite before noon.
From playful teasing to open conflict as Yuxuan refuses to hear the letters.
items.explanation: 남매는 연을 모두 팔고 편지를 되찾은 뒤 내내 웃으며 돌아올 만큼 들떠 있다. 'Then we read them' 이후 언급된 적 없는 의사 이야기가 나오고, 두 사람은 편지를 다시 묶은 채 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 따라서 성공의 흥분에서 무거운 침묵으로 바뀐다는 B가 정답이다. A는 방향이 반대이고, C는 앞부분의 일부만 다루며, D는 Yuxuan이 오히려 다시 읽어 달라고 하므로 틀리다.

items.passage: Who remembers when the old piano first lost its voice? In a school music room in Surabaya, so the story goes, two friends named Zofia and Thuy played duets on it every afternoon from the time they were small, one on the high keys, one on the low. They rarely spoke; the music did their talking. Each year another key went silent, and each year they simply played around the gap, inventing new harmonies, pretending nothing was missing. Children came to listen and clapped at the clever detours. One afternoon only a single key still sounded. Thuy pressed it, and Zofia pressed it after her, and they kept trading that one note, softer and softer, until the bell rang and neither lifted her hand from the keys.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From eager rivalry to cooperation, as the friends stop competing for keys.
From joyful celebration to bitter anger, as the piano is finally removed.
From lighthearted ingenuity in avoiding loss to a solemn acceptance of it.
From deep sadness to cheerful hope, as children gather to applaud the pair.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 친구는 소리가 사라진 건반을 피해 새 화음을 만들고 아이들이 영리한 우회에 박수를 치는 등 상실을 재치 있게 외면한다. 마지막 건반 하나만 남자 그 한 음을 점점 작게 주고받으며 손을 떼지 않는 장면에서, 끝을 엄숙히 받아들이는 어조로 바뀐다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 경쟁 관계가 없고, B는 피아노 철거나 분노가 없으며, D는 어조 변화의 방향이 반대다.

items.passage: Eunseo had warned the passenger that the ferryman's house flooded every spring, but Anders followed her down to the cellar anyway, wading through cold water to help carry up her father's boxes. He had arrived in Tromso that morning with one suitcase and no plan, and he said so cheerfully, as if it were a credential. Lifting a crate of charts, Eunseo asked why anyone would choose a town this dark in winter. Anders did not answer at once. Instead he pointed to the waterline on the stone wall, then to the older lines above it, each one marked with a year in her father's hand. 'He kept starting over down here,' Anders said. 'Every spring, the same cellar.' Eunseo looked at the marks she had passed a thousand times and, for the first time, read them as a record of persistence rather than loss.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A conflict between two characters is introduced and then settled by a compromise.
A setting is described, followed by a flashback to the father's arrival in town.
A character's plan is explained, then abandoned after a setback in the cellar.
A shared task is shown, a question is raised, and a remark reframes the familiar.
items.explanation: 글은 지하실에서 상자를 옮기는 일로 시작해, Eunseo가 왜 이 어두운 마을을 택했느냐고 묻는 질문으로 이어진다. Anders는 직접 답하는 대신 벽의 수위 표시를 가리키며 다시 시작하는 아버지의 모습을 짚고, Eunseo는 익숙한 표시를 새롭게 읽게 된다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 갈등과 타협이 없고, B는 회상 장면이 없으며, C는 Anders에게 원래 계획이 없었다.

items.passage: Paloma hated waiting rooms. She had tended the garden of the house on Calle Betis for thirty years, and she was used to hours that produced something: a pruned hedge, a bed of turned soil. Here in the hospital in Seville there was only the clock and Alba, the house's new owner, who had driven her in after the fall from the ladder. For a long time they spoke about nothing. Then Alba admitted that she had bought the house with money from a scholarship fund her late uncle had left, a fund meant for students who would now never receive it. She had wanted a garden more than she had wanted to be generous, she said. Paloma studied her bandaged wrist. 'Gardens cost too,' she said. 'Someone always pays for the shade.'
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It shows one character's impatience, presents another's confession, then a reflective reply.
It describes an accident in detail, then traces the injured character's recovery at home.
It compares two characters' careers before revealing they are rivals for the same house.
It recounts a dispute over money and ends with both characters agreeing to share the fund.
items.explanation: 글은 기다림을 싫어하는 Paloma의 성격으로 시작하고, 병원 대기실에서 Alba가 장학 기금으로 집을 샀다고 고백하는 장면으로 초점이 옮겨 간다. 마지막에는 Paloma가 손목을 바라보며 정원에도 대가가 따른다고 성찰적으로 답한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 사고를 자세히 묘사하거나 회복을 다루지 않고, C는 두 사람이 경쟁자가 아니며, D는 다툼이나 기금 분배 합의가 없다.

items.passage: Years later, I still think about the season Coach Sunethra benched me. I was the best bowler on our plantation cricket team outside Colombo, and I sulked on the boundary while she sent out girls who could barely grip the ball. Each evening after practice she walked the rows of tea with the pickers, carrying their baskets to the weighing shed, though no one paid her for it and the estate manager praised her only in speeches. I thought she was wasting her strength. One night I followed her, meaning to complain, and ended up carrying a basket myself. The pickers called me by my name, Nadeesha, as if they had always known it. Sunethra had benched me, I began to see, not to punish my arm but to show me where the team's real work happened.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a cricket match in detail, then explains why the team lost the final.
It recalls a grievance, describes a mentor's habit, then shows how joining it changed the writer.
It compares two coaching styles before arguing that the estate should pay its coaches.
It presents the pickers' complaints and then reports the estate manager's response.
items.explanation: 글은 벤치에 앉게 된 데 대한 필자의 불만으로 시작해, 보수 없이 바구니를 나르는 코치의 저녁 습관을 묘사한다. 이어 필자가 불평하려고 따라갔다가 직접 바구니를 나르며 생각이 바뀌는 과정으로 마무리되므로 B가 정답이다. A는 경기 묘사가 없고, C는 두 코칭 방식을 비교하거나 보수를 주장하지 않으며, D는 일꾼들의 불만이 등장하지 않는다.

items.passage: Wood remembers everything. Master Zihan said this whenever I, Shuang, rushed a joint in his workshop beside the abandoned orchard outside Chengdu, where his family had once grown pears. For two years I believed the orchard was simply forgotten, the trees left to split and grey because no one had time for them. Zihan's sons spoke of selling the land; his wife spoke of nothing at all. Then a furniture buyer from Shanghai came to see our tables. She walked past the polished samples, out to the orchard, and ran her hand along a fallen trunk. 'These are not neglected,' she said. 'He is drying them. This is twenty years of seasoning.' Zihan only nodded. I looked again at the rows and saw, for the first time, the careful spacing, the bark stripped in patient bands.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a carpenter's training methods, then lists the furniture a buyer purchased.
It recounts a family dispute over land and ends with the sons agreeing to sell it.
It presents a belief shared by the narrator and a family, then shows an outsider overturning it.
It contrasts two cities' craft traditions before describing the narrator's departure.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자와 가족은 과수원이 버려졌다고 믿으며, 아들들은 땅을 팔자고 말한다. 외부인인 구매자가 쓰러진 나무를 만져 보고 20년 동안 건조 중이라고 밝히자 화자는 비로소 나무의 간격과 벗긴 껍질을 새롭게 본다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 구매 목록이 없고, B는 땅을 파는 결말이 없으며, D는 두 도시의 전통을 비교하지 않는다.

items.passage: Dakar was still asleep when the author Nneka and her translator, Babatunde, sat down at the bus stop on the hill road, where an old rule was painted on a board: Wait for the third bus; the first two belong to the goats. Nneka laughed and stood when the first bus came. Babatunde did not. 'In the story my village tells,' he said, 'a herder painted that rule after his goats were nearly crushed on this bend. The goats are gone, but he did not make the rule for goats alone.' Nneka sat back down, uncertain. The first bus passed, then the second, both crowded and swaying dangerously around the curve. When the third arrived, nearly empty, she climbed aboard, opened her notebook, and asked Babatunde how the herder's words should sound in her book.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A journey is planned, a delay occurs, and the characters abandon their trip entirely.
A legend is retold in full before the narrator explains its moral to the reader.
Two characters argue about a translation until one of them quits the project.
A rule is mocked, its origin is explained, and events lead a character to reconsider it.
items.explanation: Nneka는 처음에 표지판의 규칙을 비웃고 첫 버스에 오르려 한다. Babatunde가 규칙이 생긴 마을 이야기를 들려준 뒤, 앞의 두 버스가 위험하게 흔들리며 지나가는 사건이 이어지고 Nneka는 규칙을 다시 생각해 자기 책에 담으려 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 여행을 포기하지 않고, B는 전설을 전부 다시 들려주거나 화자가 교훈을 설명하지 않으며, C는 번역을 둘러싼 다툼이 없다.

items.passage: Minjun found the gift on the shared wall between their yards on Jeju Island: a jar of honey, labeled in Younghee's careful hand, tied with red string. He tasted it at once and winced. It was buckwheat honey, dark and bitter, the kind his own hives produced, the kind he had complained about to her all summer. Still, when Younghee peered over the wall that evening, he smacked his lips and praised its depth. __She beamed and confessed that she had traded three of her best jars for it, certain he had been hinting all along.__ Minjun kept smiling. The next morning he left a jar of his own buckwheat honey on the wall, labeled in his clumsiest hand, and waited to see whether she would pretend too.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals Younghee misread Minjun's complaints, raising the stakes of his pretense.
It shows that Younghee knew all along that Minjun disliked buckwheat honey.
It explains why Minjun decides to stop keeping bees on Jeju Island at last.
It introduces a rivalry between the neighbors over whose honey sells best.
items.explanation: 앞에서 Minjun은 여름 내내 메밀꿀에 대해 불평했는데도 맛있는 척 칭찬한다. 밑줄 친 문장은 Younghee가 그 불평을 넌지시 원한다는 뜻으로 오해했고, 자기 좋은 꿀 세 병까지 내주었음을 드러내 그의 거짓 칭찬이 더 무거워지게 만든다. 이것이 다음 날 Minjun이 꿀을 되돌려 놓는 행동으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Younghee가 오해했다는 내용과 반대이고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: We set up our tables at opposite ends of the school gymnasium in Taipei, as we had for every charity fair since Zhiming opened his bakery across the street from mine. By noon his pineapple cakes had nearly sold out, as usual, and the judges were circling. I, Lanying, had come for one thing: to beat him at last. Then I bit into the sample he had left on my table, a courtesy we both pretended was friendly, and tasted salt where sugar should be. __Across the floor, Zhiming was laughing with the judges, unaware.__ I looked at the tray waiting by the judges' table, at my own lemon tarts, at the prize ribbon. Then I walked over, took his arm, and murmured that he should check his canisters before anyone else took a bite.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Zhiming deliberately ruined his cakes in order to mock the judges.
It shows that only the narrator knows of the error, setting up her choice of action.
It reveals that the judges have already chosen Zhiming's cakes as the winner.
It conveys the narrator's envy of how easily Zhiming charms the fair's judges.
items.explanation: 화자는 경쟁자를 이기려고 왔고, 샘플을 먹어 설탕 대신 소금이 들어간 실수를 발견한다. 밑줄 친 문장은 Zhiming이 아무것도 모른 채 심사위원들과 웃고 있음을 보여 주어, 실수를 아는 사람이 화자뿐이라는 상황을 만든다. 이어서 화자가 상과 쟁반을 바라보다 그에게 귀띔하는 선택으로 이어지므로 B가 정답이다. A는 의도적이라는 근거가 없고, C는 심사가 끝나지 않았으며, D는 웃는 모습에서 나온 오답이지만 문장의 핵심 기능은 '모른다'는 점이다.

items.passage: Ten slow laps in the salt-water pool off Kingston harbor: that was how my stepfather and I had always avoided talking. I was Janelle, nineteen, and he still called me 'the girl' to his friends, not unkindly. That morning we had to decide whether to move his mother, Kiara, out of the house in Port Royal where she had lived for sixty years and into our spare room. I expected him to insist; he was a man who liked decisions made. Instead, between laps, he floated on his back and told me how she had taught him to swim in this very pool, holding his chin above the water. __Then he asked what I thought she would want, and he waited for my answer.__ For the first time, I saw him not as my mother's husband but as a son afraid of choosing wrong.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows the stepfather testing the narrator before announcing a decision already made.
It explains why the family ultimately decides to keep Kiara in her house in Port Royal.
It marks a change in the stepfather's manner, showing he values the narrator's judgment.
It reveals the narrator's resentment at being asked to decide for the whole family.
items.explanation: 화자는 결정을 밀어붙이기 좋아하는 의붓아버지가 자기 뜻을 고집할 것이라고 예상했고, 그는 친구들에게 화자를 '그 아이'라고 부르던 사람이다. 밑줄 친 문장에서 그는 화자의 생각을 묻고 대답을 기다리며, 예상과 다른 태도로 화자의 판단을 존중한다. 이 변화가 마지막에 화자가 그를 두려워하는 아들로 보게 되는 계기가 되므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이미 정한 결정이 있다는 근거가 없고, B는 최종 결정이 나오지 않으며, D는 화자의 원망이 드러나지 않는다.
